transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-10-06
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: 52m
Location: Zoom
Recording ID: ff-20271006-7a9b

Attendees: Alex Miller (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Jordan Li (Redwood CSM), Marta Ruiz (NexusRetail - Head of ML), Ethan Cole (NexusRetail - SRE), Samir Patel (NexusRetail - Product), Leah Wong (NexusRetail - Security)

—— Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be fuzzy) ——
Redwood presented updated hit-rate telemetry: overall KV hit 43%, prefix reuse 31% after coalescing change, p95 latency increased slightly on cold calls. Discussed prefetch window adjustments and eviction TTL to balance cost. Customer requested a Dedicated run and security artifacts. Next: run 72h benchmark, share logs, prepare exec readout.

Transcript body:
[00:00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out the time. quick agenda — we'll run through the sprint changes to the prefetch heuristics, show the hit-rate dashboards, and then go over action items for the exec readout next week. is that still good?
[00:00:16] Marta: yep, sounds good. we got some folks on standby for the Qs.
[00:00:22] Priya: i'll start with the telemetry. so after the prefix coalescing patch we rolled friday, we're seeing aggregate kv hit move from around 37% up to 43% across the test slice. note that's an average, there's quite a bit of variance by user cohort.
[00:00:40] Ethan: can you call out which cohorts improved? was it the long session users or the short frictionless folks?
[00:00:46] Priya: good q — primarily the long session group, the ones with multi-turn product discovery flows. prefix reuse jumped to 31% there vs 18% baseline. short sessions actually dropped a little — likely because the coalescer merged prefixes and evicted some micro-prefixes earlier than before.
[00:01:05] Samir: hmm ok that aligns with what we saw in metrics — conversions didn't dip but the absolute token cost did change.
[00:01:10] Priya: right. p50 latency stayed ~85ms, but p95 crept from 220 to 260ms on specific cold-worker cases, i suspect tvl around eviction.
[00:01:22] Leah: from a security perspective we should be explicit about the logs you collect. the sample you shared yesterday had some user identifiers in meta; we need sanitized samples for any benchmark.
[00:01:33] Alex: noted. we'll scrub PII and provide a redacted sample.
[00:01:38] Priya: quick callout — we tuned the prefetch window to 3 tokens longer to capture common prompt suffixes; that helped hit for the discovery cohort but introduced a slight warmup overhead for the cold calls.
[00:01:53] Marta: what's the net cost delta? you said hit-rate improved but we saw some token increase.
[00:01:58] Priya: early estimate is about 12-18% cost reduction for the targeted cohort after amortizing the warmup penalty — but that's model and traffic dependent. for your slice the projected net unit-cost delta is ~14%.
[00:02:12] Ethan: what's that projection anchored to — hosted production numbers or dedicated sim?
[00:02:16] Priya: those are extrapolated from hosted sim runs; different kernel schedules on Dedicated could change tail numbers. that's why we recommend a 72-hour dedicated benchmark.
[00:02:27] Alex: going to the canary vs dedicated question — i know you asked yesterday about Dedicated capacity. the benefits for this pilot would be deterministic throughput and easier p95 control. tradeoff is higher baseline cost but lower variance.
[00:02:40] Marta: our execs care about predictability more than micro cost. if Dedicated gives a reliable p99 under SLO we can justify it.
[00:02:47] Samir: timeline-wise we want a readout to leadership on the 14th, so a 72-hour run that finishes by the 12th gives time to synthesize results.
[00:02:57] Alex: perfect. we'll target that — Redwood can provision a small Dedicated pool for the run. Priya, can you scope it?
[00:03:04] Priya: yes — i'll put in the config: batch=8, max-seq=1024, maintain KV snapshot across warm starts, and enable prefix coalescing. i'll also capture token-level traces for root-cause of high p95 events.
[00:03:18] [00:03:18] Ethan: one practical ask — we'll need SSO access for the infra and a sanitized traffic dump. i'll follow up with the exact bucket permissions.
[00:03:27] Jordan: i'll send the onboarding checklist and link to the shared drive after the call.
[00:03:32] Priya: quick tangent on eviction TTL — we experimented with adaptive TTL based on session length. that reduced eviction churn but increased cache memory footprint. for the pilot i recommend a middle ground: 7s baseline TTL with adaptive 0.5x shrink for very short sessions.
[00:03:50] Marta: can we quantify memory change? our infra team worried about footprint on multi-tenant nodes.
[00:03:56] Priya: roughly +18% memory for the 7s adaptive vs previous 3s static TTL on the slice we tested. but hit-rate gains offset cost for high-value sessions.
[00:04:07] Alex: also note that K-V keys are sharded and we can pin hot keys to keep cross-tenant noise down — that's part of the Dedicated config.
[00:04:15] Leah: on the compliance side, we need a KMS integration plan. does Redwood support customer-managed keys in Dedicated?
[00:04:22] Alex: yes, we support bring-your-own KMS/HSM for Private and Dedicated. we'll share the integration doc — there's a brief checklist for key rotation and audit logging.
[00:04:32] Leah: great, please add the HSM cert and an outline of audit log retention.
[00:04:38] Priya: switching back to hit-patterns — i want to flag tokenization boundaries. we saw cases where token split mid-entity caused prefix mismatch and reduced reuse. simple fix was to normalize prompts to canonical whitespace/token boundaries before cache keying.
[00:04:55] Samir: is that risky for fidelity? we can't change user-visible prompts.
[00:04:59] Priya: no, it's strictly key normalization for cache indexing — the model still receives the original prompt.
[00:05:05] Marta: ok good.
[00:05:07] [00:05:07] Ethan: digging into the p95 spikes — any hypothesis?
[00:05:11] Priya: two main suspects: eviction storms when a host restarts and KV rehydration, and some pathologically large prompts that cause kernel fallbacks. both are fixable; rehydration can be smoothed with staggered snapshots and delayed warmup.
[00:05:26] Alex: we've got a suggested runbook for rehydration and also a mitigation where Redwood streams partial KV to reduce cold penalty.
[00:05:34] Marta: how invasive is streaming partial KV?
[00:05:37] Priya: minimal — it's a runtime toggle. it increases network chatter a hair but reduces cold p95 by ~40% in our tests.
[00:05:45] Leah: want to make sure it's compatible with our VPC egress rules. we'll need a network diagram.
[00:05:50] Alex: i'll attach the diagram to the drive.
[00:05:55] Priya: we also tried prefix length heuristics — instead of fixed-length prefixing we use semantic boundaries (sentence breaks, punctuation). that raised reuse in verbose prompts.
[00:06:08] Samir: any measurable effect on relevancy?
[00:06:11] Priya: negligible, i.e., model outputs unchanged. it's purely a cache keying strategy.
[00:06:16] Marta: ok, shifting to risks — what would prevent success for us?
[00:06:21] Alex: three things: one, if your traffic mix is very short-session heavy we won't get the expected hit-rate uplift; two, if kernel fallbacks occur often on your model variant, p95 will be hurt; three, if security requires air-gapped infra we need time for Private deployment.
[00:06:36] Samir: we have a mix but skew toward discovery flows — feels promising.
[00:06:40] Ethan: about the model variant — we're on an LLaMA-derived internal fork. do you support custom model binaries?
[00:06:47] Priya: yes, we can load customer-built checkpoints. we may need a short onboarding test to validate operator kernels and quantization compatibility.
[00:06:56] Marta: timeline for that test?
[00:06:59] Priya: typical turnaround is 3-5 business days once we have access to the artifact and a small inference harness.
[00:07:06] Alex: okay let's talk deliverables. Jordan, you'll own the readout deck, Priya will run the Dedicated 72h, Ethan will provide sanitized logs and infra access, Marta to confirm success criteria. any objections?
[00:07:20] Jordan: all good from my side. i'll include a slide on enterprise risks and mitigation.
[00:07:26] Leah: we'll need the SOC2 checklist and a list of exported artifacts with retention windows.
[00:07:31] Alex: we'll attach the security pack (SOC2 artifacts, KMS integration guide, audit log spec).
[00:07:37] [00:07:37] Samir: pricing question — if we move to Dedicated for the pilot what rough delta should we budget for?
[00:07:43] Alex: for a small Dedicated pool with 4 GPUs the delta vs hosted baseline is roughly 1.6x in committed spend but you get 30-50% lower variance and better p99. exact numbers depend on usage and burst policy.
[00:07:58] Marta: can you provide a line item estimate we can share with finance?
[00:08:02] Jordan: yes i'll prepare a draft estimate and send it by EOD tomorrow.
[00:08:07] Priya: one more technical detail — we noticed key duplication in logs due to client-side micro-variations (trailing whitespace, varying JSON order). we added a canonicalizer and saw immediate reuse improvement. you might want the client change as a longer-term engineering task.
[00:08:22] Samir: we'll add that to our backlog.
[00:08:25] [00:08:25] Ethan: any blockers on Redwood's side to spin up the Dedicated run?
[00:08:29] Alex: no blockers — we just need the traffic slice and an SLA on when to stop the run.
[00:08:35] Ethan: we can target a 72h slice starting 2027-10-09 00:00 UTC. i'll confirm.
[00:08:41] Priya: great. we'll also export token-level traces and a bucket of requests flagged by low-reuse so you can inspect.
[00:08:50] Marta: what does success look like? repeat: target hit-rate 55% for the discovery cohort and p95 < 250ms.
[00:08:58] Priya: understood, we'll aim for that threshold.
[00:09:02] Alex: quick note on metrics naming — we'll put the dashboards in your drive under /redwood/pilot/NexusRetail. link will be: https://drive.redwood.internal/pilots/CRM-83421 (redacted link in notes).
[00:09:16] [00:09:16] Jordan: any external vendors or competitors we should call out for the readout?
[00:09:20] Samir: finance asked whether Anthropic or Cortex provide similar prefetching primitives; mention them but emphasize Redwood's runtime controls.
[00:09:29] Priya: i'll include a slide comparing runtime levers and the expected unit-econ impact.
[00:09:35] Leah: last security ask — can you share an obfuscated sample of the audit logs before the run? we want to ensure retention windows are understood.
[00:09:44] Alex: yes, we'll push a redacted sample tonight.
[00:09:49] [00:09:49] Marta: ok — anything else from the product side?
[00:09:52] Samir: no, just want to make sure the readout speaks to conversion impact as well as raw hit-rates.
[00:09:58] Priya: noted, i'll correlate reuse with downstream token consumption and a crude proxy for cost-to-conversion.
[00:10:06] Alex: all right — quick recap then next steps.
[00:10:09] Alex: Redwood: provision Dedicated pool, run 72h from tentative 10/09, provide dashboards and token-level traces, share security pack (SOC2, KMS docs), redacted logs tonight.
[00:10:21] Marta: NexusRetail: provide sanitized traffic slice and infra access by 10/08, confirm success criteria by 10/11.
[00:10:29] Jordan: i'll own the exec deck and the cost estimate draft.
[00:10:33] [00:10:33] Priya: technical note — we'll instrument extra p99 tracing for the run. expect an add'l 2-3% CPU overhead.
[00:10:40] Ethan: acceptable.
[00:10:42] Alex: last Q — any legal/procurement flags?
[00:10:45] Leah: procurement wants a temporary MSA addendum for the pilot — minimal but they want terms around data residency and liability.
[00:10:53] Alex: ok i'll loop in legal and share a template.
[00:10:57] Jordan: i'll also include procurement contact info in the drive.
[00:11:02] [00:11:02] Marta: thanks everyone. this is helpful. looking forward to the 72h results.
[00:11:08] Alex: thanks — we'll follow up with the checklist and next steps.
[00:11:12] (call moves to Q&A and deep technical sidebars, portions omitted)
[00:20:00] [00:20:00] Priya: sidebar with Ethan about tokenization mismatches — (low volume) we documented 12 edge cases where client JSON ordering changed KV keys. fix is client canonicalizer.
[00:28:30] [00:28:30] Priya: ran an internal micro-benchmark this morning showing rehydration streaming reduces cold p95 from 430ms to 260ms on similar hardware. that's the basis for our mitigation suggestion.
[00:37:45] [00:37:45] Alex: procurement/legal quick sync — Leah, can you confirm if the MSA addendum needs a procurement review before the run?
[00:37:52] Leah: yes, but we can do a fast-track review if the pilot is non-production and we have redacted logs.
[00:38:00] [00:38:00] Jordan: i'll flag that in the deck.
[00:45:12] [00:45:12] Priya: final technical note — we'll push a small client-side lib to canonicalize cache keys; recommended but optional for the pilot.
[00:46:30] [00:46:30] Marta: okay that seems reasonable.
[00:46:34] Alex: any last items?
[00:46:37] Samir: no, thanks.
[00:46:39] Alex: we'll close — expect the redacted logs tonight, the Dedicated run scheduled tentatively 10/09-10/12, exec readout 10/14. thanks all.

End of transcript.
